clue.text: Down they go for landing-minor panics

explanation.surface: An aircraft coming in to land, with some nervous moments on board.
explanation.definitionFit: Wing surfaces lowered on an aircraft's approach are one sense; small states of agitation, as in 'getting in a flap', are the other.

clue.text: Poor erring foe, he's not one of us

indicators.note: poor implies the words erring foe are in a sorry state and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone describing a pitiful wayward enemy as an outsider.
explanation.definitionFit: An outsider from another land is not counted among the home group.

clue.text: In heaven, at a stroke ?

parts.note: a loft is a golf stroke that sends the ball high

explanation.surface: Sudden arrival in paradise, all in one moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Something up in the sky, high overhead, is up in the heavens.

clue.text: Pugilistic salmon?

parts.note: the name of a Pacific salmon, split as two words, describes a boxer's punch to the face

explanation.definitionFit: The red Pacific salmon's name, read as a phrase, is a punch landing on the face.

clue.text: Prepared for fresco work when intoxicated ?

explanation.surface: A wall painter who has been drinking on the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A wall coated ready for fresco painting has been given a lime coating; in slang, a very drunk person is also described that way.

clue.text: Such ties belong to people ? Correct

explanation.surface: Wondering whether neckwear belongs to ordinary folk, then confirming it.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a word game: put this word before 'ties' and you get something people own, possessions. The second is plain: right and fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Placed before 'ties' it makes a word for things owned; on its own it means right or fitting.

clue.text: Anyhow, Stan's on a sound correspondence course

indicators.note: anyhow means in a careless, random way, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Somehow Stan is enrolled on a solid study-by-post course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anyhow' looks like a sentence opener but rearranges STANSONA; 'correspondence course' is not postal study but a match of sounds, assonance.
explanation.definitionFit: Assonance is the matching of vowel sounds, so a word showing it follows a pattern of corresponding sounds.

clue.text: Subject : Alphonse of today

parts.note: a subject of discussion is a topic
Al is short for Alphonse, as in Al Capone

explanation.surface: A headline subject: a man named Alphonse in the news.
explanation.definitionFit: Something current and in the news concerns present-day matters.

clue.text: Controlled formation of the glue trade

indicators.note: formation suggests building something new out of the letters of glue trade

explanation.surface: Glue makers' business is set up under strict government rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Something controlled is kept under rules and supervision.

clue.text: A piece of gold in Arab countries once

definitions.text: A piece of gold in Arab countries once

indicators.note: piece of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A historical coin of gold that once circulated in Arab lands.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'countries once' as the definition, which does not define a coin; the whole clue defines it, with 'piece of' pointing to golD IN ARab.
explanation.definitionFit: The early Islamic gold coin was struck across Arab lands; the name still serves for money in several of them.

clue.text: Radical cuts in farm produce ?

parts.note: radical comes from Latin radix, so a radical part is the root
to crop is to cut short, so cuts can be crops

explanation.surface: Drastic reductions in what farms produce.
explanation.definitionFit: Turnips, carrots and beets are crops grown for their underground parts, a kind of farm produce.

clue.text: Heathen god takes in silver

indicators.note: takes in says the god's name swallows the symbol for silver

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of shepherds and the wild
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A heathen deity accepting offerings of silver.
explanation.definitionFit: A heathen is a follower of a non-Christian or polytheistic religion, as a pagan is.

clue.text: How the natives do talk!

parts.note: reads as an exclamation about chatty locals, but asks for the phrase meaning in the local everyday language

explanation.definitionFit: Speaking in the everyday tongue of a place's people is how its natives talk.

clue.text: Metal of little value in U.S.

explanation.surface: Some cheap metal from America.
explanation.definitionFit: A silvery metallic element is one sense; the American five-cent coin, worth little, is the other.

clue.text: What Mrs Grundy might do to this magazine-seller?

definitions.text: What Mrs Grundy might do to this magazine-seller?

parts.words: What Mrs Grundy might do to this magazine-seller?
parts.note: Mrs Grundy, a byword for prudishness, would want to clothe a scantily dressed young woman on a magazine front

explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Grundy is a character from an 18th-century play whose name became a byword for prudish disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: An attractive model photographed for the front of a magazine helps sell copies.

clue.text: Blows up in an unfortunate final set

indicators.note: unfortunate suggests the letters of final set are put into a bad, disordered state

explanation.surface: A player loses their temper in a disastrous deciding set of a tennis match.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow something up is to pump air into it, swelling it out.

clue.text: More mobile and urban than its namesake under the elms

definitions.text: More mobile and urban than its namesake under the elms

parts.words: More mobile and urban than its namesake under the elms
parts.note: Tennessee Williams' play title is a city tram named Desire, while O'Neill's play is Desire Under the Elms, a rural and static setting

explanation.definitionFit: A tram running on city streets bears the name Desire in the play title, more mobile than O'Neill's rural Desire.

clue.text: Had a stab, say, at the exam, and got it off one's chest ?

indicators.note: say signals that a word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: pecked means struck at with the beak, had a stab at
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A student had a go at a test and unburdened their feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' tells us PECKED is heard, giving PECT. 'got it off one's chest' plays on the idiom for confessing, but a breastplate or chest muscle comes off the chest literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the breast, as a chest muscle or a priest's breastplate, belongs to the thorax area.

clue.text: The world under love's influence is likely to end with a bang

definitions.text: likely to end with a bang

explanation.surface: Love sets the world spinning but it will all end explosively.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half leans on the saying 'love makes the world go round': a world under love's influence turns, so it is something that turns. The second is a handgun, which ends a story with a bang.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that turns round and round is one sense; a handgun with a rotating cylinder, fired with a bang, is the other.

clue.text: Before the Fringe — it's out crazy, man !

explanation.surface: Someone goes mad before the Edinburgh festival fringe starts.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half names the word that comes before 'fringe' in the phrase for an extremist minority, with a nod to the revue Beyond the Fringe; 'it's out' joins the halves.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase for an extreme minority starts with this word; on its own it means a madman.

clue.text: Webster's carriage ?

parts.note: Webster looks like the dictionary maker, but here means a web-weaving creature, and the word for it also names a light horse-drawn carriage

explanation.definitionFit: A high, light horse-drawn phaeton is known by the name of the eight-legged web spinner.

clue.text: Father's Day recreation

parts.note: pa is dad, so father's is pa's
a day as in 'in my day' is a time or era

explanation.surface: A hobby taken up for the June holiday honouring dads.
explanation.definitionFit: A hobby or leisure activity is a form of recreation.

clue.text: The Foreign Office has some light on the raids

parts.note: FO is the abbreviation for the Foreign Office, Britain's foreign ministry
rays are beams, some light

explanation.surface: The British foreign ministry shedding light on military attacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden incursions into enemy territory are raids.

clue.text: Box Street, No. 1 makes a contribution (Scotch) to the ceremony .

parts.note: Coronation Street is a long-running British TV soap, a street seen on the box (television); its name abbreviates as Coronation St
number one is one

explanation.surface: Someone at a house on a street donates to a ceremony, with an aside about whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: CORONATION STREET is a British TV soap, so the 'Box Street' is the one on the box (television), shortened to St. The Stone of Scone, taken from Scotland, sits under the throne at British coronations.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stone of Scone, brought from Scotland, is set beneath the throne at a crowning, so it is Scotland's part in the rite.

clue.text: The best colour ?

explanation.surface: Asking which shade is finest.
explanation.definitionFit: The top part, as in the elite of a group, is one sense; a pale yellowish white shade is the other.

clue.text: Watch this space, Houston

parts.note: an astronaut tells mission control in Houston to watch the region beyond Earth's atmosphere

explanation.definitionFit: The region beyond the atmosphere is called outer space, so the first word fits the phrase.

clue.text: Priest to turn poet

parts.note: Eli is the priest of Shiloh who raised Samuel in the Bible

indicators.note: turn tells us to flip the little word to so it reads the other way

explanation.surface: A clergyman deciding to take up writing verse.
explanation.definitionFit: T. S. Eliot, author of The Waste Land, is a famous poet.

clue.text: Practical amendment it is clear

indicators.note: an amendment is a change, so the letters of it is clear are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sensibly declares that a proposed change is obviously sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical person or plan is down-to-earth and sensible.

clue.text: Breakwaters contain 'the French copper particles

indicators.note: contain says the breakwaters hold the other pieces inside them

parts.note: a mole is a stone pier or breakwater
le is French for the
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Harbour walls with French copper pieces trapped in them.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest units of a compound, made of atoms bonded together, are tiny particles.

clue.text: "Sole judge of truth, in endless — hurled " (Pope)

definitions.text: "Sole judge of truth, in endless — hurled " (Pope)

parts.words: "Sole judge of truth, in endless — hurled " (Pope)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from Pope's Essay on Man, describing man as the only judge of truth yet tossed about in endless mistakes

explanation.definitionFit: Pope's line runs 'in endless' then a word for mistake, matching a wrong belief or slip.
